glossary.definition: RFC 9126. The client sends the authorization request parameters straight to the authorization server over an authenticated back channel and gets back a short-lived, one-time request_uri. The browser then carries only client_id and request_uri.
A reference to a pushed request, such as urn:ietf:params:oauth:request_uri:abc. It is short-lived (60 seconds here), single-use, and bound to the client that pushed it.

What the agent or user is asking to do: the action, the amount and currency, and the resource it applies to, plus a nonce. The authorization server binds it at PAR time and every later hop checks it is unchanged.
Holding the intent on the server from PAR onward and tying it to the consent, the code and the token by hash, so a token only works for the exact thing the user approved.
RFC 9396 Rich Authorization Requests. A JSON array that says in structured form what a token is for. This mock copies the bound intent into it.
A client setting (require_pushed_authorization_requests in RFC 9126). When on, the authorization endpoint refuses any request that does not use a request_uri.
A token issued for one intent executes it once. A second run, even of the same action, is refused by the resource server.

stories.title: Push, approve, execute: the intent travels intact
stories.say: The intent is pushed once, held by the server, shown to the user, copied into the token, and checked again when the token is used.

stories.title: The agent proposes, the human approves the exact intent
stories.say: The approval is for one specific action. The same token cannot be reused for a dearer one, a different target, or a second run.

stories.title: Amount edited in the browser link
stories.say: With PAR, parameters beside request_uri are refused, so editing the link cannot change what was pushed.

stories.title: Approval submitted for a different intent
stories.say: Consent is bound to the intent hash. An approval that names a different intent is refused, so a swapped consent screen cannot launder an approval.

stories.title: Resource swapped at the token request
stories.say: A token request may not change the bound intent. The server compares it with what was pushed and approved.

stories.title: Valid token, different target
stories.say: A genuine token is still only good for its own intent. The resource server compares what is attempted with the bound intent.

stories.title: Valid token, bigger amount
stories.say: The approved amount is a ceiling that is also a floor: the action must equal the intent, not merely stay under a scope.

stories.title: request_uri replayed
stories.say: A request_uri is one-time. Whoever sees it in a log or history cannot use it again.

stories.title: request_uri used after it expired
stories.say: A pushed request lives for 60 seconds. A stale link is useless.

stories.title: request_uri presented by another client
stories.say: A request_uri belongs to the client that pushed it.

stories.title: Pushed request with no intent
stories.say: This server will not issue authorization without knowing what it is for.

stories.title: Inline parameters when PAR is required
stories.say: When a client is set to require PAR, an authorize request with inline parameters is refused outright. That is what makes PAR enforceable.

stories.title: Contrast: no PAR, the link can be edited
stories.say: Without PAR the intent rides in the browser, where it can be changed. The server binds whatever arrives, so the token faithfully carries the edited intent.

stories.title: Token edited to raise the amount
stories.say: The intent claim is signed. Editing it breaks the signature.

stories.title: Unregistered parameter in the push
stories.say: This server is strict: parameters it does not know are refused rather than silently ignored.
